\[
E = \sum_i \left( \alpha \lvert v_{i+1} - v_i \rvert^2 + \beta \lvert v_{i+1} - 2 v_i + v_{i-1} \rvert^2 \right) + \sum_i P(v_i),
\qquad
P = -\left( w_{line} \, Y_\sigma + w_{edge} \, \lvert \nabla Y_\sigma \rvert \right)
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(v_i\): Point i of the snake
- \(\alpha\): The elasticity
- \(\beta\): The rigidity
- \(P\): The image energy
- \(Y_\sigma\): The luma after a Gaussian blur of sigma

The snake is a closed chain of points, called v. Its energy E has an internal part and an image part. The alpha term is small when the points are close, so it pulls the chain tight. The beta term is small when the chain is straight, so it resists bending. With a positive line weight, the image energy P is low on bright pixels. With a positive edge weight, it is low on edges. Y sigma is the blurred luma, and its gradient comes from the Sobel filter. Each step solves for the internal forces with a fixed matrix, as Kass, Witkin and Terzopoulos did, and moves down the image energy. The scikit-image code limits each move to the largest move. It stops when the snake is within the settled distance of one of its 10 saved positions.
